housing: Nuneaton and Bedworth grew on coal mining and textiles, so Victorian and Edwardian terraces fill the streets around both town centres, especially in Abbey and Chilvers Coton. Post-war council-built estates such as Camp Hill (now being regenerated) sit alongside large private estates from the 1960s to the 1980s at Whitestone and St Nicolas Park. Private renting grew quickly between 2011 and 2021, mostly in the older terraces, and large new-build estates are being added on the edges of Nuneaton.
checkinTips: Victorian terraces in Abbey and Chilvers Coton: photograph damp at the base of walls, back yards, rear alleys and outhouses.
Flats over shops in Nuneaton and Bedworth town centres: record the separate entrance, stairs, meter location and fire escape.
Former mining terraces in Bedworth and Stockingford: photograph any cracks or uneven floors and the state of gutters and downpipes.
New-build estates on the edges of Nuneaton: note snagging marks, sealant, parking spaces and new fences and turf.
1960s–80s estate homes in Whitestone and St Nicolas Park: photograph older windows and doors, garages and boilers.
tenantHelp: Tenants can report disrepair, damp or unsafe conditions in privately rented homes to Nuneaton and Bedworth Borough Council's private sector housing team.
